title: Why Do the Wealthy Wicked Boast
description: Why Do the Wealthy Wicked Boast in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 37, part 2, headed “Charity to the poor; or, Religion in words and deeds”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Why do the weal-thy wi-cked boast, And grow pro-fane-ly bold? The mean-est por-tion of the just Ex-cels the sin-ner's gold.

lines: Why do the wealthy wicked boast,
And grow profanely bold?
The meanest portion of the just
Excels the sinner's gold.
The wicked borrows of his friends,
But ne'er designs to pay;
The saint is merciful and lends,
Nor turns the poor away.
His alms with liberal heart he gives
Amongst the sons of need;
His memory to long ages lives,
And blessed is his seed.
His lips abhor to talk profane,
To slander or defraud;
His ready tongue declares to men
What he has learn'd of God.
The law and gospel of the Lord
Deep in his heart abide;
Led by the Spirit and the word,
His feet shall never slide.
When sinners fall, the righteous stand,
Preserv'd from every snare;
They shall possess the promis'd land,
And dwell for ever there.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
